claim: Board of review meets annually during the 45-day period beginning on the 4th Monday of April, no sooner than 7 days after the assessment roll's last open-for-examination day.
Notice of intent to object must be given to the board clerk (written or oral) at least 48 hours before the board's first scheduled meeting, subject to good-cause waiver during the first 2 hours.
A written objection must be filed with the board clerk within the first 2 hours of the board's first scheduled meeting (waivable only for extraordinary circumstances).
DOR must receive a written complaint within 20 days after delivery of the board of review determination, or within 30 days after the mailing date on the clerk's affidavit.
cite: 2026 Guide for Property Owners (WI DOR), sec. X.E.2 (sec. 70.47(12))

claim: A board of review determination may be appealed by certiorari to circuit court within 90 days after receiving notice from the board.
cite: 2026 Guide for Property Owners (WI DOR), sec. X.E.1 (sec. 70.47(13))

claim: A claim for excessive assessment must be served on the municipal clerk (or county clerk in a county assessor system) by January 31 of the year the tax is payable.
The municipality must allow or disallow an excessive assessment claim within 90 days; if disallowed, the claimant has 90 days after receiving notice to sue in circuit court.

Assessment ratio is the relationship between a parcel's assessed value and its fair market value (e.g., $140,000 assessed on a $150,000 sale is 93%); assessment level is the district-wide assessed-to-equalized-value relationship.
cite: 2026 Guide for Property Owners (WI DOR), Glossary

An exempt homestead of a resident owner who occupies it is exempt from execution, judgment liens and creditor debts up to $75,000, except mortgages, mechanics' and purchase money liens and taxes.
The exemption extends to sale proceeds up to $75,000 while held with intent to procure another homestead, for 2 years.
Each spouse may claim up to $75,000 on land owned jointly or as marital property.
A conveyance that alienates a married person's interest in a homestead must be signed (or joined in) by each spouse, except conveyances between spouses.

A real estate transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value (or fraction) is imposed on the grantor on every non-exempt conveyance.
For land contracts, the value is the total principal amount the buyer agrees to pay the seller.
The register of deeds collects the fee when the deed is submitted for recording; a completed transfer return signed by grantor and grantee is a prerequisite to recording.
Transfer returns filed on or after July 1, 2009 must be filed electronically as prescribed by the Secretary of Revenue (waivable for undue hardship).
Twenty percent of fees stay with the county; the balance goes to the state.

Exempt conveyances include: transfers for nominal or no consideration between parent/child, stepparent/stepchild, grandparent/grandchild; between spouses; by will, descent or survivorship; TOD transfers; value of $1,000 or less; foreclosure or deed in lieu to a mortgagee or land contract seller; delinquent-tax sales; partition.
Local fees on conveyances exempt from the state transfer fee are prohibited.

Wisconsin foreclosure is judicial: judgment adjudges the mortgaged premises be sold, with sale by sheriff or referee.

For owner-occupied 1-4 family residences, farms, churches and nonprofits with a mortgage executed on or after April 27, 2016, sale may occur upon expiration of 6 months from entry of judgment; first notice printing no earlier than 4 months after judgment.
If the mortgagor shows a good-faith effort to sell and has a broker listing agreement (motion before judgment), the waiting period is 8 months (first notice printing no earlier than 6 months).
Mortgages executed before April 27, 2016 on those property types carry a 12-month period (first notice printing no earlier than 10 months).
If the lender waives deficiency (20 acres or less, mortgage executed on/after April 27, 2016), sale occurs after 3 months (5 months with a listing agreement).
Commercial and multifamily (other than owner-occupied 1-4 family) foreclosure sale may not be held until 6 months after judgment (3 months if deficiency waived).
The mortgagor may redeem at any time before the sale (confirmation) by paying the judgment amount, interest, costs and any taxes paid by plaintiff.
Abandoned premises: sale can be held after 5 weeks from judgment, and must occur within 12 months.

Notice of an in-person foreclosure sale is given under s. 815.31 and must include the property street address and judgment sum.
Execution sale of real estate must be advertised by posted written notice at least 3 weeks before the sale, plus a notice printed weekly for 3 successive weeks in a county newspaper.
The sheriff or referee may not accept less than $100 as a deposit or down payment; the balance is paid to the clerk of court on confirmation; the purchaser pays the cost of sale.
Within 10 days after sale the sheriff or referee files a sale report and delivers the deed and proceeds to the clerk of court, who holds the deed until confirmation.
Court confirmation is required; if the sale price is below the debt, no presumption of fair value and the court may not confirm until fair value is credited on the debt.
Purchaser must pay transfer fee, recording fee and the remaining price within 10 days after confirmation.
A county may require Internet-based auctions for foreclosure sales by ordinance.
Third-party bidders must meet minimum qualifications (e.g., no property with taxes more than 120 days delinquent) and the buyer files an affidavit before confirmation.

Summary settlement/transfer by affidavit is available where the decedent's property is $50,000 or less in gross value; petitioners include an heir, trustee of a revocable trust, or nominated personal representative.

Interest of a decedent in real property, a land contract vendor interest, or a mortgage may be confirmed through an application to the register of deeds (surviving spouse, TOD beneficiary, etc.); no dollar limit is stated in s. 867.046.
The application requires the property tax bill, legal description, and a copy of the deed creating a joint tenancy, life estate or TOD interest; recording terminates the decedent's interest.
If the spouse/beneficiary has not started a confirmation proceeding within 90 days after death, any interested person may apply.
A good-faith purchaser or lender from a petitioner takes title free of estate claims and has no duty to inquire about the propriety of the transfer.
A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt from the transfer fee.
Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-supervised fiduciaries who have never occupied the property are exempt from the seller condition report.
